changedSections.question: Using rounded dry-air nitrogen 78 %, oxygen 21 %, argon 0.9 %, CO₂0.04 %, calculate their volumes in an invented 500 cm³ sample. Must the four numbers sum exactly 500, or describe mass percentages?
Why does an airtight oxygen-removal model use excess moist iron and sufficient time? Is the remaining gas pure nitrogen or must all the iron react?
For a supplied teacher-controlled P₄ model, balance P₄ + O₂ → P₄O₁₀. Why should the gas be cooled before comparing volumes, and can P₂O₅ replace the product with the same coefficients?

An invented fixed flask/tube contains 80 cm³ gas, and its syringe changes 40→16 cm³ after complete oxygen removal at matched temperature/pressure. Calculate the whole-sample estimate; why is 24/40 wrong?
An oxygen-removal plan stops early, measures the final gas while warmer and compares column lengths in a tapered tube. Explain the likely issues and why close repeats do not remove them.
Balance Mg + O₂ → MgO and explain why retained oxide can have greater mass than the reacting magnesium. Does bright light alone prove a sample burned in air is pure MgO?

In an invented particle model, six H₂ molecules and four O₂ molecules react, forming only water until all hydrogen is consumed. Use 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O to count water molecules and unreacted oxygen. Check both atom totals; is carbon dioxide possible from these starting particles?
A supplied equation represents sulfur as S₈. Balance combustion to SO₂. Does consuming oxygen guarantee a comparable fall in total gas volume to the moist-iron experiment?
For supplied basic copper carbonate CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂, write its balanced thermal decomposition and explain why the pure CuCO₃ model omits a product. Is added oxygen required?
Correct “CO₂ creates heat, stops every wavelength escaping and a cold week disproves its climate effect”. Distinguish the ozone mechanism.
